title: Data Landscape Scanner
summary: A data discovery and governance system supporting 40+ technologies for cataloguing, lineage, and classification.
role: Worked across connectors, security hardening, metadata discovery, and scanner optimization.
problem: Enterprise teams needed one reliable way to discover, classify, and trace data assets across a wide mix of databases, warehouses, BI tools, and cloud services. Coverage gaps, inconsistent metadata discovery, and security concerns made governance difficult at scale.
solution: The platform was expanded to support broader technology coverage, stronger metadata discovery, and safer query execution. Work included improving scanner behavior for key cloud platforms, expanding connectors, and strengthening security posture so cataloguing and lineage could remain dependable as adoption grew.
responsibilities: Built and improved connectors for systems including dbt, Kafka, and Power BI.
Mitigated SQL injection risks and tightened scanner-side query safety.
Implemented tag discovery for database objects to improve classification workflows.
Optimized scanner behavior for Azure Synapse, Databricks, and Snowflake.
results: Expanded discovery coverage across a broader set of enterprise technologies.
Improved governance readiness with stronger classification and tagging support.
Reduced operational risk by hardening query execution and connector behavior.
Made lineage and cataloguing more dependable for large heterogeneous estates.
description: The Data Landscape Scanner project revolutionizes data discovery and governance by supporting over 40 technologies, including Oracle, Snowflake, AWS Glue, and Tableau. Built on Java with Akka Streams, it enables efficient data stream processing and customization through user-defined queries. My contributions include mitigating SQL Injection vulnerabilities, enhancing connectors, and implementing tag discovery for database objects, ensuring robust data organization and classification. Additionally, I optimized scanners for Azure Synapse, Databricks, and Snowflake, while building connectors for dbt, Kafka, and PowerBI, enabling seamless data cataloguing and lineage across platforms.

title: Unified Data Platform (UDP)
summary: A platform for designing and deploying big data pipelines without exposing users to infrastructure complexity.
role: Built backend platform capabilities, Airflow integrations, quality controls, and automated testing coverage.
problem: Data teams needed a way to build and deploy ETL workflows without taking on the full operational burden of orchestration and infrastructure. At the same time, the platform had to stay reliable under production pressure, improve visibility into execution, and raise engineering quality across multiple repositories.
solution: Core backend features were designed to make pipeline creation, orchestration insight, and platform operations more dependable. The work combined product delivery with engineering quality improvements, including resilient APIs, orchestration integrations, automated end-to-end coverage, and stronger CI quality gates.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented backend features for ETL and notebook-related workflows.
Integrated Airflow visibility to expose deeper insight into job and pipeline execution.
Resolved production issues within strict SLAs while keeping sprint delivery on track.
Automated complex end-to-end ETL testing and introduced SonarQube quality controls.
results: Improved platform reliability and day-to-day delivery confidence for data teams.
Reduced manual validation effort through stronger automated coverage.
Raised code quality and coverage across repositories while addressing critical issues.
Lowered security and maintenance risk through better CI and code-health discipline.
description: UDP (Unified Data Platform) provides a comprehensive solution for designing and deploying big data pipelines, along with additional features for efficient management. It abstracts infrastructure complexities, enabling UDP users to focus on their core tasks, such as creating ETL jobs and deploying them on managed Airflow. I was responsible for ensuring the timely delivery of sprint commitments without escalations, which included designing and implementing core backend features for an ETL data pipeline project, such as fault-tolerant APIs, Notebook APIs, and Airflow integration to provide deep insights into job and pipeline execution within orchestration platforms, while resolving critical production issues within strict SLAs. I automated testing for complex end-to-end ETL use cases, significantly reducing manual effort, and ensured code quality by integrating SonarQube into CI/CD pipelines, eliminating P1 issues, mitigating security vulnerabilities, and increasing code coverage from 10% to 80% while minimizing OWASP vulnerabilities across multiple repositories.

title: Error Reprocessing Tool
summary: A system for monitoring and recovering data migration failures in near real time.
role: Helped improve observability, recovery workflows, and operational reliability during migration work.
problem: During migration from on-prem systems to Azure, teams needed a reliable way to identify, analyze, and recover from failures quickly. Without focused observability and controlled recovery paths, errors could slow migration progress and increase operational risk.
solution: The platform centralized error visibility and supported both automated and manual recovery paths so teams could react quickly to failures. The work focused on making the monitoring and reprocessing flow dependable enough for live migration operations.
responsibilities: Supported monitoring and analysis flows for migration-related failures.
Improved recovery behavior for both automated and operator-driven reprocessing.
Contributed to overall platform reliability for near real-time operational use.
Helped shape a workflow that reduced friction for engineering teams handling migration incidents.
results: Improved observability for migration failures in near real time.
Reduced recovery friction through clearer reprocessing paths.
Lowered migration delivery risk with more dependable operational tooling.
Made error handling more structured for cloud migration teams.
description: ERT is a purpose-built platform for Data Engineers and Cloud Developers to monitor, analyze, and reprocess system errors during data migration from on-prem systems to Azure Cloud. It provides a reliable, scalable way to track errors in near real-time and offers both automated and manual recovery options, improving observability and reducing migration risk.

title: Core Payment Services Platform
summary: A full digital payments platform covering card activation, transactions, fee handling, and notifications.
role: Worked end-to-end across backend services, frontend integration, deployment, and production support.
problem: The platform needed to support the full digital payment lifecycle while staying dependable for both customer-facing flows and business-critical transaction handling. That meant features had to move from planning to production smoothly across backend services, UI integration, infrastructure, and support.
solution: Features were delivered across the payment lifecycle with an end-to-end mindset, covering service development, interface integration, deployment, and live support. The work balanced product delivery with operational responsibility so payment functionality could remain stable under real usage.
responsibilities: Built and maintained backend services using Java, Spring Boot, and Spring Cloud.
Handled frontend integration needs through server-rendered UI work with Thymeleaf.
Worked with AWS services such as SQS and EC2 during deployment and delivery.
Took features through planning, implementation, release, and production support.
results: Supported dependable payment workflows across multiple stages of the user journey.
Improved delivery continuity by handling both implementation and operational follow-through.
Enabled business-critical features to ship with clearer end-to-end ownership.
Strengthened the platform's day-to-day reliability for production payment operations.
description: I worked as a full stack developer on the Core Payment Services Platform, a suite of services that supported the full digital payment lifecycle—from card activation to transaction processing, fee handling, and user notifications. My work included backend development, frontend integration, and deployment on AWS, with a focus on delivering features that directly impacted end users and business operations. On the backend, I used Java, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, and AWS services like SQS and EC2. For UI needs, I used Thymeleaf to build server-rendered pages. I was responsible for developing and maintaining features end-to-end, from planning to production support.
